cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: T3, T4, T5 each answer a named prior claim; T7 answers T6's 14-day step.
cells.limitation: T1 and T2 open independently; T8 and T9 leave T7's cost objection unanswered.

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T7 adds that silence may read as the user's own withdrawal.
cells.limitation: T7's and T8's new distinctions are never used by a later turn; T9 restates.

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: T8 sets comfort with friend as-is against needing proof of investment.
cells.limitation: Saying something, the user's actual option, is never debated in T1-T9; only section E.

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T6 Existentialist drops his claim after T5's secure-base point.
cells.limitation: T6 concession looks forced; Smith's mutual-sympathy point (T4) never reshapes anyone.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: T9 sharpens the question: accept the friendship as is, or require change.
cells.limitation: Ending question was nearly available at T1; little narrowed on whether to speak up.

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T4 restates T3's action claim accurately before objecting.
cells.limitation: T5 reduces T3 to 'just act differently'; T3 recasts T1 as waiting for reciprocity.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T7 names the cost: silence read as withdrawal, friend retreats further.
cells.limitation: T4 and T7 objections go unanswered by their target; T5 objection asserts rather than tests.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: T4 'mutual sympathy of sentiments' fits Smith's Theory of Moral Sentiments.
cells.limitation: Suspected stretch: T5 applies Bowlby's child-caregiver secure base to adult friendship unqualified.

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: T9 separates disputed readings: lack of care versus communication style.
cells.limitation: Hedges in nearly every sentence, yet Situation asserts an anxiety the user never stated.

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T6 explicitly concedes to T5 and drops its earlier claim.
cells.limitation: T6's new step does not follow from the concession; T7's objection to it never answered.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern, including ambiguity about what the user is really asking
cells.example: Section E finally weighs a direct, non-accusatory conversation.
cells.limitation: Debate turns are about testing by waiting, not whether to say something.

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: T7 uses 'lovely connection' to price the cost of a waiting test.
cells.limitation: Only two user details exist and neither changes the argument beyond T7.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: T8 asks which matters more: comfort as-is or proof of investment.
cells.limitation: T6 pushes its own 14-day test; the user's question about speaking up is sidelined.

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: T7 names the stake: ending a lovely connection out of pride.
cells.limitation: Situation invents anxiety; T2 invents the friend's lack of reliable responsiveness.

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: T8 poses one value question that section E branches on.
cells.limitation: Never asks duration, whether the friend always accepts, or whether the user raised it before.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: T8 offers comfort-as-is versus proof of investment with an answerable question.
cells.limitation: Situation states anxiety as fact; T5 asserts 'the safety you crave'.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: T9 questions whether silence means no care or a different style.
cells.limitation: The assumption that initiation equals caring surfaces only at T9, unexamined earlier.

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: T8 names conflict between a secure base and freedom to stop initiating.
cells.limitation: Value of honesty in speaking up never weighed against these in T1-T9.

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: T2 calls fear of drift a natural response; T7 names pride.
cells.limitation: T5's 'safety you crave' leans toward pathologising an ordinary wish for reciprocity.

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: Section D asks whether user would still enjoy always starting conversations.
cells.limitation: T6 prescribes waiting exactly 14 days rather than offering a distinction to weigh.

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options, including waiting, learning more, or a limited step
cells.example: Section E lays out accept, talk, or wait-and-observe.
cells.limitation: The talk option is absent from every turn; no lighter way of mentioning it.

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs in terms that matter to the user; no option treated as costless
cells.example: T7 prices the wait: friend may read silence as withdrawal.
cells.limitation: Cost of a direct conversation is never stated; section E treats it as costless.

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: Section E branches on whether user prioritises enjoyment or mutual effort.
cells.limitation: Conditions are preferences, not observables; T6's 14 days has no basis in user facts.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: Section D names the key unknown: indifference or lack of initiative.
cells.limitation: Minor unknowns not separated; friend's circumstances never considered as an unknown.

cells.name: Proportionate next steps that follow from the analysis and fit the constraints
cells.example: Section E suggests a non-accusatory conversation about feelings.
cells.limitation: Section E endorses the 14-day wait despite T7's unanswered cost; no wording guidance.

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: T8's closing question is plain and directly answerable.
cells.limitation: 'Secure base' (T5) and 'mutual sympathy of sentiments' (T4) left unexplained.

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T3, T4, T5 name the mind and claim they answer.
cells.limitation: T6's reasoning from T5's point to the 14-day step is untraceable.

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: Nine turns, all within 25 to 65 words per checks.
cells.limitation: Every turn the same length and shape; no short, sharp exchange varies pace.

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices, with explicit changes of position
cells.example: T6 marks an explicit change of position.
cells.limitation: All three minds share one hedging 'might' register; T2 and T5 sound like T1.

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: Section E compresses the options into three branches.
cells.limitation: T3, T4, T5 open by restating the prior claim; T9 recaps rather than adds.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension arising from the issue itself
cells.example: T7: risk of ending a lovely connection out of pride.
cells.limitation: Stakes stay abstract; no turn imagines the actual conversation or its fallout.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals that stay plausible. ★ A reversal the text traces to an earlier turn's argument, naming what changed the speaker's mind. A change of position with no stated cause is a template, not a reversal
cells.example: T6 Existentialist drops his claim, citing T5's secure-base point.
cells.limitation: T6's cited cause does not explain the new 14-day test; reversal reads scripted.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice without caricature
cells.example: T3: 'you are creating the friendship through your choices'.
cells.limitation: Flat, hedged register in all minds; no Smithian wit or Sartrean edge.

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: T7's pride framing is the sharpest line.
cells.limitation: No analogy, vivid example or humour anywhere in T1-T9.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement, with varied rhythm rather than constant intensity
cells.example: T7 interrupts the drift toward waiting with a concrete cost.
cells.limitation: Constant even register T1-T9; T9 ends on a flat recap.

strengths: T8 Attachment Theorist names a real value conflict with a question the user can answer.
T7 Moral Observer prices the 14-day wait: silence may read as the user's withdrawal.
Section E turns the T8 question into three conditional branches.
weaknesses: Whether and how to say something, the user's question, is absent from T1-T9.
T6 Existentialist proposes an ungrounded 14-day test after a concession that does not lead to it.
All three minds share one hedging register; voices and positions blur from T1 to T9.

symptoms.observed: No turn debates speaking up; the asked option appears only in section E.
symptoms.evidence: have a direct, non-accusatory conversation about your feelings

symptoms.observed: Proposes a fixed waiting period with no basis in the user's facts.
symptoms.evidence: wait exactly 14 days before reaching out again

symptoms.observed: Never asks history, friend's acceptance pattern, or prior conversations; speculates instead.
symptoms.evidence: the silence you fear might be their way of signaling

symptoms.observed: Every mind hedges with might or may; registers indistinguishable.
symptoms.evidence: You might want both a secure base and the freedom

symptoms.observed: T7's cost objection to the 14-day step is never answered; section E endorses it.
symptoms.evidence: carries the cost of potentially ending a lovely connection

findings.description: Situation asserts a persistent anxiety and T2 a friend's unreliable responsiveness; the user stated neither.
Bowlby's secure base, developed for child-caregiver attachment, is applied to adult friendship without qualification.
Smith attributions on reciprocity and mutual sympathy are paraphrases with no source evidence attached.

rubric_fit_notes: Rubric fits a relationship decision. The user's question is short, so C3.2 has little personal context to use; ratings judge use of what was given plus what was left unasked.
raw.question_type_note: As a decision question, every cell was read as written, with saying something taken as the central option.
